errors.english: Thus, if life itself is the (Pradhana), then that too becomes hollow.
errors.why: སྲོག is evidently a corruption of གསོག: the result posited in the pradhāna, being hollow, makes that too hollow; 'life itself' is not in the argument.

errors.english: one examines the (Pradhana) through the result, which has the nature of potency
errors.why: The Tibetan says the result is posited (imagined) in the pradhāna in the form of a potency, not that the pradhāna is examined through the result.

note: Follows the Sāṃkhya refutation in outline, but the core argument about the result-as-potency in the pradhāna is muddled in two places.

errors.english: In solitude, I would loosen my girdle with my hands, yet she would completely restrain me.
errors.why: The lover fantasises loosening HER girdle while she resists; it is not his own girdle.
རྒོད་པ is playfulness/excitement (auddhatya), not rāga; the supplied equivalent is wrong.

errors.english: and suffer through the senses that roar with sound
errors.why: The phrase opens a description (continued on the next side) of evil-doers made pitiable by their wailing cries; 'senses that roar' is invented.

note: A difficult kāvya passage rendered in readable prose, with some misreadings of who does what and a garbled final sentence.

errors.english: "the sign of the third is certainly established."
errors.why: The phrase concerns the triple-formed (trirūpa) sign being established as known, not 'the sign of the third', and 'certainly' is not here.
ཁྱེད་ཅག are the Buddhist treatise-makers addressed by the objector, not the opponents.

note: The anvaya/vyatireka argument and the role of 'eva/niścita' are rendered accurately apart from a muddled opening.
The apoha argument is followed correctly; some clumsy phrasing (the question on negating apoha) and unmarked inline glosses, but nothing that changes the meaning.
A faithful rendering of the bhūtagrāma pāyattika commentary, with the seed classes, creatures and the analysis of the offence correctly given.

errors.english: Their reversal is the non-existence of non-perception.
errors.why: Their absence is the non-existence that consists in (is known by) non-perception, not the non-existence of non-perception.

errors.english: Since it is possible for a cause to exist without the result, this also thoroughly expresses the answer
errors.why: 'Since a cause can exist without its result' is part of the objection being answered, not the author's own reason.

errors.english: by using arguments that the body and mind are not incompatible with such states
errors.why: The Mīmāṃsakas use reasons such as having a body and intellect, which are not incompatible with omniscience; the non-incompatibility is Dharmakīrti's diagnosis, not the content of their argument.

note: The anupalabdhi discussion is followed in outline, but several sentences misassign or invert the logical roles.

errors.why: The verse says that, because the reason consists in the avinābhāva relation, it never lies in the three modes; it does not say that the three modes never exist separately.

errors.english: the necessity that the effect cannot exist without the cause
errors.why: This is an unmarked, and too narrow, gloss: anyathānupapatti is not limited to cause and effect.

errors.english: The engagement does not occur because of certainty.
errors.why: It means that even with the three modes the reason does not lead to certainty, not that certainty prevents it.

errors.english:
Are non-existent in every way
Because they are not perceived in any way
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར་ཡང = kathaṃcit, 'in some respect'; the (Jaina) thesis is that things are non-existent in some respect, not in every way; the same applies to the parallel 'exist ... in every way'.

errors.english: Even if the property of the subject (paksadharmatā) is a non-entity,
errors.why: It means that even when there is in fact no pakṣadharmatā, the reason is seen to make known.

note: Verse form is kept, but several of Pātrasvāmin's key claims against trairūpya are distorted.
A faithful rendering of the momentariness argument, including the variant reading.

errors.why: The lemma (continuing རྒྱུན་ from the previous side) says 'because [destruction] is of the nature of the cutting-off of the continuum'; གང་ཡིན་པས is not interrogative.

errors.english: When it is explained in relation to a vase and so forth
errors.why: Here འཆད་པ means ceasing: when a vase is said to cease, the meaning is that it does not arise again.

note: The two kinds of destruction and the account of contradiction are rendered soundly, with two misread lemmas.
A faithful word-by-word rendering of the commentary's glosses on the tigress episode.
